I have farmed this land a long time, so I will not change too much. On 5 mu, fertilizer is real money, but losing yield costs more, so I will keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steady way here with well water. I will put 4 mu into wheat first, then summer maize on that same 4 mu after harvest, and I will keep 1 mu for cotton. That is close to what people around me do: keep the grain land steady and leave a smaller piece for cotton. With my age and only 2 people in the house, I will also choose methods that save labor, so I will use rotary tillage for wheat, no-tillage or simple direct sowing for maize after wheat, and plough once for cotton land to make it clean at the start.

For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put a solid base fertilizer, and give 3 irrigations if the season is normal: one after sowing if moisture is short, one at greening or jointing, and one around heading or filling. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because the yield is better and most neighbors do the same now; I will feed it a bit heavier on nitrogen because maize eats fertilizer and I do not want thin ears. For cotton, I will not put too much land because it takes more watching and more spraying, but I will still grow 1 mu and feed it enough so bolls do not run small. I will spray cotton more times than wheat and maize because insects on cotton are troublesome here. I will keep rates a little on the safe side this year, not low, because with irrigation I can still push for a decent harvest.
